title: Data types: choosing values, initialization, and measuring a target
goal: Choose a type for a value and observe integer versus floating-point division.

prerequisites.text: You know integer expressions, % and !=; this step introduces double and bool.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: A type determines values and operations. int holds integers, double holds approximate real values, bool holds false/true, and char holds one encoding unit, not an arbitrary letter in every language. Five whole items divided between two people have integer quotient 2; 5.0/2.0 gives 2.5.

5.0 is a floating-point literal. In contrast, 5/2 performs integer division before any result is stored elsewhere. Sizes and exact limits depend on the platform: do not infer every pointer size from one machine. Signed integer overflow is not a valid way to obtain the “next” number.

sections.title: Choose a type for a value and observe integer versus floating-point division.
trace: The fractional part is not part of the integer quotient.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: Replace 5 with 6 in both divisions, keeping .0 for double.
hasRemainder still asks about 5! Change it separately too; then the final number becomes 0.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: double value = 5/2 gives 2, not 2.5: the destination type does not recover a discarded fraction.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Compare 7/2 and 7.0/2.0. Print both results and a bool indicating whether 7 has a remainder.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

terms.definition: Rules for an object’s values and operations; a type does not necessarily encode domain units.
Providing an initial value when an object is created. Here every object is explicitly initialized.
The set of representable values: a finite numeric type cannot hold every mathematical number.
The environment for which a program is built, including type representation and library; browser Clang/WASM is one particular target.
An operator reporting size in C++ bytes. sizeof(char) is 1; CHAR_BIT gives the number of bits in such a byte.
A standard-library facility exposing arithmetic-type properties of the selected implementation.
An acceptable error chosen for a task, not a universal guarantee of double accuracy.

blockPracticum.title: Practicum A: a panel batch report
blockPracticum.label: FIRST-BLOCK PRACTICUM
blockPracticum.starterLabel: Starter with an explained unit conversion
blockPracticum.challenge: Build a reproducible report for 4 panels of 125 cm: category A, approved true, 500 cm, and 5 m. Preserve evidence for the four introductory skills.
blockPracticum.readiness: Begin when you can explain the main scaffold, choose unit-bearing names, distinguish const/constexpr, and initialize simple types. Division by the double factor is supplied as an explained scaffold before the conversions lesson.
requirements: stdin is empty: initial quantities are explicit and explained.
Five lines: category=A, approved=1, length_cm=500, length_m=5, cm_per_m=100.

panelCount is bounded to 0…100 and panelLengthCm to 0…1000: the product is at most 100000; long long covers this range. long long is a two-word integer type name; the rest of the declaration uses the same syntax.
The reference variants use whole meters: 0 panels and 8 panels of 125 cm. General rounding and full input parsing are outside this task.
milestones: Write the contract and independent calculation before coding.
Add a character label, flag, reason comment, and missing output lines.
Check the main and two changed scenarios.
Attach a target report and rubric-based self-review.
walkthrough: Count × centimeters per panel gives total centimeters. Division by the double factor produces a floating-point result. For our small values the conversion is exact; general rules follow later.
Choose long long for the product: its guaranteed range covers 100000. The minimum range of int alone does not promise this. Reason about bounds before running instead of experimenting with overflow.

constexpr double centimetersPerMeter{100.0}; stores the fixed factor as a floating-point value. It is used both in the calculation and in the report. Compared with the earlier constexpr int declaration, only the selected type and literal have changed.
artifacts: main.cpp with meaningful names and one reason comment.
A table of expected and actual stdout for three scenarios.
A target report distinguishing guarantees from observations.
A self-review and one diagnosed defect with a repeat check.
